summary: Drove the full task-level terrain surface end to end on a live desktop engine (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001). Built + uploaded aether_kit.wasm, loaded MarkBook, TerraEditor (config via mark_book_mailbox), and WorldView. Created a named Path mark (id 1) and Point mark (id 2) with terrain_marks; selected both and relabeled them "surveyed" through TerraEditor (revisions bumped 1->2). Staged a brush proposal from the Path mark (proposal 1, source_mark geometry, rev 2), set it as the preview, captured a frame (green chevron following the ridge-path — visible only after loading a camera and using an orbit view), and committed it. Staged an automaton (grow) proposal from the Point mark (proposal 2) and discarded it. Retried apply_terrain_brush with a stale MarkRef (Path id 1 rev 1) — rejected at preflight ("operator source mark reference is stale", MCP -32602) with no world mail sent; the final capture is byte-identical to the committed frame, proving no mutation. All component results projected the documented named-record vocabulary (Created/Applied/Staged/Committed/Discarded, {value} mark ids, revisioned MarkRefs). Everything succeeded through the public tool surface; the friction was almost entirely in discovery/onboarding, not the tools' operation.

artifact.rationale: The captured frame shows a single contiguous green brush-stroke terrain — a smooth curved/checkmark-shaped path — on a dark slate background. This matches the expected path-derived brush terrain that the preview and post-commit frame should both display. There is no scattered/cellular point-derived automaton pattern visible, consistent with the discarded automaton proposal producing no committed visual change. The stale-reference rejection is a structured tool-error concern, not a pixel one, so it has no bearing on this visual verdict.

papercut.what: Passing the identical JSON {"mark_book_mailbox":"mbx-ma5o-wbdl-owam"} inline via the `config` argument failed with 'config does not match aether.kit.terra.config: field "$" expected object', but writing the exact same bytes to a file and passing `config_path` succeeded. The docs present the two as equivalent (mutually exclusive, same schema-encode). The inline path appears to mangle the object (encoder sees a non-object at root $).
papercut.suggested: Fix aether-mcp so inline `config` is schema-encoded the same as `config_path`, or document the divergence. This silently pushes users to files for no reason.

papercut.what: TerraEditor's config needs the MarkBook's runtime MailboxId, which only exists after MarkBook is loaded (returned as a tagged mbx- string). This forces a strictly sequential load (can't preload both via spawn_substrate/boot-manifest since the sibling's mailbox id isn't known at boot), and it's non-obvious that the tagged mbx- string is even an accepted config value (it is, but only via config_path — see the inline-config bug).
papercut.suggested: Document that mark_book_mailbox accepts the MarkBook LoadResult name/mailbox_id and must be loaded first; or let TerraConfig accept a MarkBook load-name string that the editor resolves, so the two can be co-loaded.

papercut.where: aether.kit.camera set_mode Orbit (incidental camera needed for the render)
papercut.what: The Orbit mode struct fields (distance/pitch/yaw/speed/fov_y_rad/target) are all Option in the schema, but the codec rejected the mail with 'missing required field "$.mode::Orbit.0.speed"' unless every field was supplied. Optional-in-schema but required-by-encoder is surprising and cost a round trip. (Off the terrain surface, but hit while setting up the required render.)
papercut.suggested: Make the encoder honor Option (omitted -> None) for struct fields inside enum variants, or drop the Option from these fields if they are truly required.

doc-gap.where: Onboarding to the whole terrain surface (docs/guide has no terrain page; SUMMARY.md lists none)
doc-gap.what: The guide's only terrain material is one dense paragraph in mcp-harness.md plus ADRs 0142/0143. To actually use the surface I had to read crate internals: the component selectors (aether_kit@aether.kit.mark / .terra / .world) come from crates/aether-kit/src/lib.rs export! and the NAMESPACE consts; the mandatory TerraConfig{mark_book_mailbox} requirement and its type come from terra/kinds.rs; the load ordering (MarkBook first, capture its mailbox, then configure TerraEditor) is undocumented. A fresh consumer working from docs + public signatures cannot discover any of these.
doc-gap.suggested: Add a docs/guide/recipes/terrain-authoring.md walkthrough: which selectors to load, that TerraEditor requires TerraConfig.mark_book_mailbox pointing at the MarkBook's LoadResult mailbox_id, the load order, and a minimal marks->select->propose->preview->commit script.

doc-gap.what: A brush proposal is flat (all height 0, a thin material overlay). With the default booted camera the capture is blank, and my first instinct — a top-down camera aimed at origin — also rendered completely blank (a flat overlay is edge-invisible / not framed by topdown). Only an orbit camera pitched downward showed the terrain. The terrain surface offers no viewable-camera helper and no doc pairing preview/capture with a camera, so a fresh user sees a blank frame and cannot tell whether the proposal or the camera is wrong.
doc-gap.suggested: In the terrain recipe, show the exact camera setup for previewing terrain (orbit, downward pitch, target at the mark centroid) and note that top-down over a flat overlay renders nothing. Consider a convenience 'frame these marks' camera helper.

doc-gap.what: Coordinates are in 'octimeters' but no conversion is documented. I authored a path spanning 0..160 octimeters expecting ~20m (1/8 m each); the returned digest bounds were ~0.85m total, so the effective scale is nothing like 1/8 m and is unpredictable, making it impossible to author marks at a known world size or to pre-plan a camera extent.
doc-gap.suggested: State the octimeter->meter conversion in the tool docs / recipe and give the visible world size of a sample mark so users can frame it.
